title: VLSM
description: Different subnet sizes in one network
tagline: Different subnet sizes in one network

sections.title: The Problem VLSM Solves
sections.body: Plain subnetting gives every piece the SAME size. A LAN needs 100 hosts, but a router-to-router link only needs 2 — giving it /26 wastes 60 addresses. VLSM (Variable Length Subnet Mask) lets each piece get its own right-sized mask.

sections.title: The Golden Rule: Biggest First
points: Sort requirements from LARGEST to smallest.
Give the biggest network the first block.
Next subnet starts where the previous one ended.
Use /30 for every point-to-point router link.

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.body: From 192.168.1.0/24 give: Sales 100 hosts, HR 50 hosts, IT 20 hosts, one WAN link:
sections.code:
/25 = 126 hosts -> Sales : .0   - .127
/26 = 62  hosts -> HR    : .128 - .191
/27 = 30  hosts -> IT    : .192 - .223
/30 = 2   hosts -> WAN   : .224 - .227
(wasted space? almost none!)

sections.title: Subnetting vs VLSM
sections.tip: 💡 Exam tip: always start from the largest requirement or you will create overlapping subnets.
